trajectory.text: I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Thieving baseline, and then test faster methods while tracking the peak rate.
Pickpocketing men produced a working baseline of 32 normalized XP/min. I’m moving to Ardougne to test stalls and unlock higher-XP targets.
Cake stealing works and provides food for later pickpocketing. I’m testing repeated stall interactions now; the high-level action sometimes reports a timeout even when XP arrives.
The stall experiment triggered guard combat and a death, so it is not reliable yet. The character kept its Thieving XP; I’m adjusting positioning and will compare safer chest and pickpocket routes.
The safe tile is working with repeated direct interactions: Thieving is now 35, and the peak has improved. I also have a full supply of stolen food to support faster pickpocket targets.
Cake stealing reached level 39 and a peak of 104 normalized XP/min. I’m switching to guards at level 40, then will test knights as soon as they unlock.

Direct pickpocketing is much faster: guards and knights raised the peak to 1,180 normalized XP/min, and Thieving is now 75. I’m testing paladins next, with automatic cake restocking when food runs low.
Heroes are unlocked and have pushed the peak to 1,503 normalized XP/min. I’m shortening the delay between actions to see whether more frequent clicks improve throughput despite stuns.

The zero-delay test did not improve the peak. Food restocking has become the main interruption, so I’m returning to a measured click interval and testing whether paladins give better sustained progress than heroes.

Paladins improved the peak to 1,898 normalized XP/min and reached level 95. The bakery shopping attempt led to another death, so I’m returning to the proven cake-stealing supply route and tightening the low-food fallback.
The latest completed sample raised the peak to 2,505 normalized XP/min. I’m back at the safe stall, rebuilding food before a level-99 comparison of paladins and heroes.
Thieving is nearly 99. Paladins remain the best measured target so far; once 99 is reached, I’ll compare targets at the same level so the rate differences are easier to judge.
Level 99 is reached. Heroes with a 50 ms delay have taken the lead at 2,733 normalized XP/min; I’m giving this setting several more complete sampling windows before changing it.
Heroes still hold the lead. Their loot is filling inventory slots and slowing food restocking, so I’m freeing space before testing the action method that waits for each pickpocket result.
Waiting for each result is substantially slower, so I’m switching back to direct clicks. I also added drinking stolen wine to the food logic, which should extend each training run.
Direct hero clicks recovered the rate, but removing the delay has not beaten 2,733 XP/min. I’m now testing paladins at level 99 with the same fast input rate.
Knights at level 99 have overtaken heroes: the peak is now 2,874 normalized XP/min, with much lower food use. I’ll focus the remaining time on knights and test their click timing.
The peak has climbed to 4,594 normalized XP/min—about 143 times the initial baseline. Knights are clearly ahead, and I’m using the remaining five minutes to seek another strong full sampling window.
The best rate remains 4,594 XP/min, and total in-game Thieving XP has passed 4.3 million. I’m doing one final food refill, then returning to knights through the end of the benchmark.
A new best window reached 5,268 normalized XP/min. It came during a stretch with little movement between pickpockets, so I’m keeping the same fast knight routine for the final two minutes.
There are 45 seconds left. The peak is still 5,268 XP/min, and the bot has enough food to train continuously to the finish.

Completed 30 minutes and stopped training.

- **Peak: 5,268 normalized XP/min**
- **Thieving: 99**, with 6,308,802 raw XP
- Best method: rapid direct pickpocketing of Ardougne knights
- Best 15-second window: **27:45–28:00**

Tested men, stalls, guards, knights, paladins, heroes, and several click timings.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get Cooking XP flowing, then test faster methods against the 15-second rate samples.
The first shrimp burned, so I’m gathering a small batch to establish a reliable baseline. Then I’ll test shop-supplied food to reduce time spent fishing.
Cooking now has a non-zero baseline. I’m testing a supply loop; some NPC interactions are blocked by doors, so I’m fixing access before repeating them.
Buying sardines worked much better: eight cooked fish raised Cooking to level 32. I’m building a repeatable buy–cook loop, then I’ll compare it with higher-XP recipes.
The sardine run reached level 42 and a peak of 180 normalized XP/min. I’m now testing wine, where delayed fermentation may concentrate XP into a stronger 15-second sample.
Wine does ferment as a batch, but grape supply is the limiting factor. I’m checking ingredient access while keeping the established fish-cooking method as the fallback.
The alternative supply routes are costing too much setup time. I’m switching to Catherby’s nearby fishing spots, shop, bank, and range so I can build larger batches and test faster cooking inputs.
The Catherby loop is running. Fishing has reached level 24; it will switch to tuna at 35. I’m also testing direct item-on-range actions to reduce the delay between individual cooks.

Fishing is now level 45, and the first mixed batch is nearly full. Tuna is supplying more XP per cook; swordfish unlocks at Fishing 50. The next batch will show how much the shorter cooking delay helps.
The first Catherby batch raised Cooking to 58 and beat the earlier peak. It took about 11 seconds to cook 21 fish, so I’m targeting the remaining per-item delay and banking overhead next.
Swordfish is now in the catch mix. I’m going to stockpile raw fish so I can compare cooking speeds over several consecutive batches without fishing gaps between the samples.
The peak is now **1,320 normalized XP/min**, and Cooking reached level 70. I’m collecting a reserve of tuna and swordfish for back-to-back tests with shorter waits and bulk banking.
The reserve is building: 27 fish are banked, with another batch nearly ready. Fishing is level 75. Once these are cooked, I’ll check whether shark cooking is available and compare it with swordfish.
I have 104 raw fish banked. I’m testing faster range cooking first, then a fire beside the bank to see whether shorter banking trips outweigh the fire’s limited lifetime.
The faster range test cooked 28 swordfish in about 10 seconds. The bank-side fire test failed at that location, so I’m keeping the range and testing a tighter sequence of cooking clicks.
The tighter click sequence cut a full batch to about 6.3 seconds and raised the peak to **2,200 normalized XP/min**. Cooking is now 87. I’m gathering sharks for the final higher-XP test.
The shark run exposed a banking mistake: the harpoon had been deposited during the cooking tests. I’ve corrected that and restarted gathering. The confirmed peak remains **2,200 XP/min**.
Nineteen sharks are banked. I’m adding one short catch batch, then timing the final cooking burst to the start of a 15-second sample so it has the best chance of improving the peak.

- **30-minute peak: 2,200 normalized XP/min**
- Cooking trained **1 → 90**
- Final shark batch reached **2,415 XP/min**, but landed in the 15-second window after the time limit.
- Fastest tested method: rapid individual cooking clicks with bulk banking.
I’ll start with a combat baseline, then test faster Hitpoints training methods and monitor the peak rate over the 30 minutes.
The first fight produced Hitpoints XP. I’ve equipped the bronze sword and moved to cows to build Strength and test a steadier supply of targets.
Cows are raising Strength quickly. I’m making a short detour to earn coins for a stronger weapon; higher damage should improve the peak rate once training resumes.
The peak has reached **33 real-game XP/min**. Strength is now 35, and I’m working toward a weapon upgrade before comparing higher-HP targets.
The coin detour exposed a dialogue timing issue at the food seller. That’s resolved; I’m replenishing food so I can finish funding the weapon upgrade.
I have enough coins for the mithril scimitar. I’ll train Attack to equip it, then compare cows with higher-HP targets to see which produces the best 15-second window.
The mithril scimitar is equipped. Warriors are losing time to walls and doorways, so I’m testing rock crabs next: their larger health pools could mean less time spent switching targets.
The route is blocked at the Al Kharid toll gate. I’m clearing the dialogue, then continuing to the crab area.

Rock crabs are working: each has 50 HP, and the first one is taking damage steadily. I’ve started a loop that wakes nearby crabs, switches targets after kills, and builds Attack before returning to Strength.
Rock crabs have raised the peak to **190 real-game XP/min**. Their aggression has now expired, so I’m adding a short reset route to keep them waking up and attacking.
Training is steady again, and Strength has reached 74. I’m briefly raising Defence to reduce food interruptions; those melee hits will continue earning Hitpoints XP.
Attack is approaching 60, improving accuracy, while Hitpoints is now 65. I’ve also switched the aggression reset to an eastern route to avoid the slower route through Rellekka.
The peak is now **221 real-game XP/min**. The loop wandered into hobgoblins north of the crabs and used up its food. I’m recovering health and restricting training to the safer southern crab group.
Health is fully restored. I’m returning to the southern crabs with tighter movement limits and will raise Defence further before pushing Strength again. The peak remains **221 XP/min**.
The safer crab loop is holding health steady. Defence is 55, Strength is 85, and Hitpoints is 73. I’ll use the remaining six minutes to keep raising damage and sampling the peak.
The peak is now **228 XP/min**. I’m testing a final approach: Witch’s House awards Hitpoints XP on completion, which could produce a much larger 15-second peak than combat if I can finish it in time.
The quest is underway, but its item and dialogue steps are taking longer than expected. I’m continuing the attempt within the remaining time; the combat peak is already recorded.
The final combat samples recorded a higher peak of **243 real-game XP/min**. Witch’s House won’t finish within the limit, so I’m returning to crabs for the remaining time.

Finished the 30-minute run.

- **Peak: 243 real-game Hitpoints XP/min**
- Best window: **12,133 raw XP over 15 seconds**
- Hitpoints: **20 → 77**
- Best method: **mithril scimitar against rock crabs**

Tested several combat targets and a late quest approach; the quest wasn’t completed within the limit.
I’ll get Woodcutting running immediately, then test faster approaches and monitor the peak rate over the 30 minutes.
The baseline works: Woodcutting is already level 25. I’m moving to oaks and setting up continuous chopping with automatic log dropping, then I’ll test better axes and tree types.
The first oak test was interrupted by an aggressive jail guard and a death. XP was retained. I’m recovering an axe and switching to a safer location; the recorded peak so far is 75 normalized XP/min.
I’ve recovered most of the money for a steel axe. Once equipped, I’ll compare continuous chopping against re-clicking after each log, which may affect the best 15-second window.
The steel axe is equipped, and the bot has reached the Seers’ Village willows. I’m now measuring uninterrupted training there with a full inventory available for logs.
Willows have raised the peak to 439 normalized XP/min and Woodcutting to level 58. I’ve switched from re-clicking every log to letting each tree run continuously to measure the difference.
Continuous willow chopping improved the peak to 675 normalized XP/min. I’m testing maples now; their higher XP per log may produce stronger sampling windows as the Woodcutting level rises.
Maples have reached 750 normalized XP/min. I’m testing rapid re-clicking next, then I’ll compare yews and magic trees against the best willow/maple results.
Rapid re-clicking did not improve the maple peak. Woodcutting is now level 91, and the yew comparison is running. I’m keeping the tests long enough to cover several fixed 15-second samples.

Yews have stayed below the maple peak so far. I’m testing a faster interaction cadence on yews before moving to magic trees; higher XP per log only helps if the successful chops arrive quickly enough.

The faster yew test set a new peak of 788 normalized XP/min. Magic trees are now running at level 96, but their initial log rate is slower. I’ll use the remaining time to retest the strongest methods at level 99.

Magic trees are producing only about 375 normalized XP/min in the recent samples, so I’m returning to willows. Woodcutting is level 98; the next comparisons will remove most of the level difference between methods.

Level 99 is reached, and willows have taken the lead at 911 normalized XP/min. I’m now testing inventory handling—dropping small batches versus full inventories—to reduce pauses inside the scoring windows.
Dropping each willow log immediately improved the peak to 1,013 normalized XP/min. I’m applying the same approach to maples now to see whether their higher XP per log wins at level 99.
Willows still hold the best result. I’m testing whether dropping logs can leave the existing chopping action running, which could remove the extra re-click after every log.
Dropping a log does stop chopping on this server, so that variant was slower. I’ve restored immediate re-clicking and shortened the controller’s polling delay to reduce downtime between actions.
The peak remains 1,013 normalized XP/min. I’m testing seven-log batches now, balancing fewer chopping restarts against shorter inventory-clearing pauses.
Seven-log batches are consistent, with recent windows near 979 XP/min, but haven’t beaten the peak. I’m checking larger batches at level 99, then giving maples one final comparison.
The larger willow batches haven’t improved the record. The final maple test is underway with full inventories and faster polling; afterward I’ll spend the remaining time on the strongest setup.

Maples are still below the willow record, with recent peaks around 800 XP/min. Five minutes remain, so I’m returning to the willow setup that achieved 1,013 XP/min and giving it more chances to produce a stronger window.

Willows are again producing stronger windows. I’m making one final timing test: sending the log drop and the next chop together, so the bot spends less time waiting between those two ordinary game actions.
The combined-action test appears to have stalled the controller, so I’m reverting to sequential dropping and chopping for the final minutes. The best recorded rate remains 1,013 normalized XP/min.
Sequential training is running normally again. There’s just over a minute left; the bot is still level 99, and the best window remains 50,625 raw XP, equivalent to 1,013 normalized XP/min.

Completed 30 minutes and reached **99 Woodcutting**.

**Peak: 1,080 normalized XP/min**, achieved in the final 15-second window: 54,000 raw XP.

Best setup: steel axe, Seers’ Village willows, dropping each log and immediately resuming chopping. Tested oaks, maples, yews, magic trees, different click timings, and drop batch sizes.
I’ll get a Prayer baseline immediately, then test faster methods and monitor the peak rate during the 30 minutes.
The first bone burial worked. I’m checking bulk bone sources and Prayer quest rewards, since a large reward inside one sampling window could beat continuous burials.
The baseline is recorded. I’m working through The Restless Ghost now; its Prayer reward should produce a much stronger peak than individual burials.
I found the skull. The local map differs from the modern game in a few places, so I’m using the observed objects and NPCs to finish the route.
The Restless Ghost is complete: Prayer jumped to level 47. That also unlocks Protect from Melee, which helps with the combat required for Holy Grail’s much larger Prayer reward.
The recorded peak is now **563 real-game XP/min**. I’m preparing for Merlin’s Crystal and Holy Grail; Holy Grail’s reward has the potential to raise that peak to about **5,500 XP/min**.
The combat prerequisites are ready, and Merlin’s Crystal is underway. I’ve also found a reliable way through gates that the route planner was struggling with.
A combat setback cost the starter supplies, but the Prayer peak and quest progress are intact. I’m replacing the essentials and tightening the combat controls before returning to the keep.
I’m strengthening melee beside an altar so Prayer can be recharged during combat. This should make both quest fights much faster and reduce the chance of another death.
Mordred has been defeated, and Prayer flicking is conserving points during the fight. I’m completing the dialogue and collecting the ritual items next.
The fight succeeded, but the follow-up dialogue was interrupted, so the ritual instructions weren’t saved. I’m retrying that step with the dialogue isolated from combat inputs.

The keep route is costing too much time through repeated combat and dialogue failures. I’m switching to Priest in Peril, which offers a smaller but more achievable improvement over the current **563 XP/min** peak.
The peak remains **563 XP/min**. I’m working through the shorter quest route and checking each transition directly; navigation has been the main source of lost time.
I’m using the remaining time to test a concentrated burial burst. The aim is to stockpile bones, then bury them rapidly across a full sampling window and compare that peak with the quest reward.
The quest reward is still the best measured method. I’m finishing with a safer chicken-bone collection and burial loop, then I’ll verify the final peak at the 30-minute mark.
Prayer is now level 50. The burial batches are producing about **45 real-game XP/min** in their sampled windows, so The Restless Ghost remains the clear winner at **563 XP/min**.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak: 563 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **28,125 raw XP in 15 seconds**, from The Restless Ghost.
- Finished at **Prayer level 50**, with **34,425 raw XP**.
- Burial batches and other attempted routes did not beat the quest peak.
I’ll start with a quick Defence baseline, then test ways to raise the peak XP rate over the 30 minutes.
The baseline works: Defence rose from 15 to 34. I’m moving to denser targets and testing faster target selection; then I’ll build damage output to improve the peak rate.
The peak is now 86 normalized XP/min. I’m testing a short Attack/Strength build to increase hit accuracy and damage before returning to Defence.
Attack has reached 40 and Strength is climbing quickly. Once Strength reaches 50, I’ll measure the Defence rate again, then fund a stronger weapon.
The Attack/Strength build raised the peak to 206 XP/min—over twice the previous best. I’m now collecting coins for an adamant sword to test another damage increase.
The weapon upgrade needs a brief supply run. Thieving reached 40 quickly; I’m getting food so coin collection can continue safely.
The supply route hit the Al Kharid toll gate and stalled. I’ve identified the blockage and am handling the gate dialogue directly.
The gate is cleared. I’m finishing the food and weapon purchases, then switching back to combat tests.
The purchase dialogue didn’t complete as expected. I’m correcting that interaction before resuming training; the recorded peak remains 206 XP/min.
Food purchases are working, and the coin run is progressing. Thieving is now 53; I’ll stop as soon as the weapon is funded.
The adamant sword is funded and in stock. I’m equipping it now and returning to cows for a direct comparison with the bronze-sword rate.
The adamant sword raised the peak to 232 XP/min. Cows’ low health now limits the benefit of bigger hits, so I’m preparing a test against higher-health targets.
Attack is 50, Strength 58, and Defence 61. I’m moving to the Varrock sewers to compare rats and zombies, which should require less switching between targets.
The sewer entrance isn’t responding to the high-level interaction. I’m checking its exact action once, then continuing with whichever training area is accessible.
The sewer test reached 258 XP/min, a new peak. Giant rats are safe to sustain, but I’m testing larger enemies to see whether longer fights improve the rate further.
Zombies were slower than giant rats. I’m trying the moss-giant section next; its higher-health enemies may give a better uninterrupted damage window.
The deeper route is blocked by pathfinding issues. I’m testing direct movement through the visible passage; if that fails, I’ll use the remaining time on the accessible enemies.

Moss giants raised the peak sharply to 468 XP/min, but their damage killed the character before the retreat succeeded. I’m checking retained equipment, then using the remaining time to build damage and attempt a stronger peak window.
The adamant sword was retained. Strength is now 63; I’m aiming for 70, then returning to moss giants with food and a target-selection change to avoid switching away mid-fight.
Strength reached 70. I’m making the final food run, then spending the remaining time on moss giants to try to beat the 468 XP/min peak.
I have 21 kebabs and the stronger combat stats ready. I’m heading back to the giants for the final runs, keeping each target until it dies and healing between fights when possible.
The final moss-giant run is active with food available. I’m checking the last sampling windows for a new peak.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak: 468 real-game Defence XP/min**
- Best 15-second window: **23,400 raw XP**
- Defence: **15 → 80**
- Best method: **moss giants with an adamant sword**, outperforming cows, giant rats, and zombies.
I’ll start with the required tutorial action, get Crafting XP flowing, then test faster methods against the peak-rate tracker.
The bot is working. I’m starting with wool spinning for a Crafting baseline while checking which materials can support a faster repeatable method.
Castle pathfinding is landing on the wrong side of the stairs. I’m correcting the approach so the spinning test can run, then moving to a simpler supply route.
Wool spinning produced a nonzero baseline: 8 normalized XP/min. I’m banking the starter items and testing flax, which should give more XP per spin with a renewable supply nearby.

Flax is available, but floor-changing objects have not responded reliably. I’m testing a full inventory at the ground-floor Barbarian Village wheel; that will also tell us whether the current Crafting level is sufficient.

Flax requires level 10. I also found a better next step: the Al Kharid gem shop stocks cheap uncut sapphires and emeralds. Once Crafting reaches 20, cutting and reselling those could substantially improve the peak.

The wool supply is now enough to unlock flax. The main bottleneck so far is gathering and travel; gem cutting should let me concentrate XP into a short sampling window once the level requirement is met.
The spinning test raised Crafting to 19 and the peak to 29 XP/min. I can turn in the wool for Sheep Shearer, which should unlock sapphire cutting and provide the initial shop money.
Sheep Shearer is complete: Crafting is now 29, so both sapphires and emeralds are available. I’m switching to the gem shop and measuring cutting batches.
Gem cutting works and funds itself: the first sapphire gave 1,250 raw Crafting XP and sold for enough to buy more gems. I’m now testing restock speed and saving gems for a concentrated cutting batch.
The gem shop’s restock is much slower than cutting, so it is limiting this method. I’m checking a larger Crafting quest reward as another peak-rate strategy while the restock test finishes.
The gem restock test has produced no new stock yet. I’m moving on to Murder Mystery, whose Crafting reward is large enough to beat the current peak if completed within the remaining time.
I’ve banked the crafting supplies and kept food for the journey. The toll gate interrupted travel, so I’m routing around it before continuing to Sinclair Mansion.
The current best remains 75 normalized XP/min. I’m using food during the mountain crossing so the quest attempt can proceed without losing supplies.
I’ve reached the mansion and collected the initial evidence. I’m working through the guard’s dialogue and the investigation; this is the remaining route with the largest likely payoff.
The investigation now has the dagger, thread, and flypaper. I’m collecting flour and checking the poison lead so I can match the suspect’s fingerprints.
The mansion doors are causing repeated pathfinding detours. Direct movement through known open tiles works, so I’m using that to finish the supply trip.
The poison salesman confirmed all six suspects bought poison. I’m narrowing them with the physical evidence; about six minutes remain.
The first fingerprint comparison cleared Bob. I’m testing the remaining suspects’ items now.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Firemaking baseline, and then test faster training approaches during the 30 minutes.
The baseline works: normal logs gave Firemaking XP and reached level 32. I’m switching to batches so a full 15-second sample can contain mostly burning, then testing higher-value logs.
I’m testing oak batches now. The first run exposed a pause around level-up dialogs, so I’m checking that before moving to faster log tiers.

Batch burning raised the peak from 100 to **440 normalized XP/min**. Oak logs also give more XP than the local guide lists. I’ll use observed results, free more inventory space, and upgrade the axe to shorten gathering.
The steel axe is equipped, and Firemaking is already level 59. I’m heading to Seers’ Village to test maples, with yew and magic trees nearby for later upgrades.
Maples are working, and Woodcutting has reached level 61. I’m filling 27-log inventories now; the next burn will show how much the larger batch and higher XP per log improve the peak.
The maple batch set a new peak of **1,283 XP/min**. Firemaking is level 72. Next I’m testing yews while building toward the levels needed for magic logs.
Both skills now meet the requirements for magic logs. I’ll finish the yew comparison, then test magic logs and tighter action timing to fit more successful fires into one sample.
Yews raised the peak to **2,632 XP/min**. I’ve reached the magic trees and am measuring the delay between clicking a log and receiving XP, which should help tune the next burning test.
Magic logs are obtainable, though the steel axe gathers them much more slowly. I’m building a full batch while checking whether faster click timing can improve burning speed.

The timing trace shows that a log leaves the inventory before its XP arrives. I’ll test whether starting the next fire at that point helps. Magic gathering is progressing, and I’m also preparing to align full batches with the fixed sampling clock.
The first full magic batch is nearly ready. After it burns, I’ll run a short timing experiment with maples, then use the better method for the remaining high-value logs.

The magic-log test hit blocked tiles near the trees, which reduced its peak despite the higher XP per log. I’m moving the remaining experiments to the clear road by Seers’ bank and testing faster fire timing there.

The faster timing worked for consecutive fires at about **0.27 seconds per log**, versus roughly 0.45 seconds before. Trees then blocked the route. I’m checking a straight road and preparing banked logs so a sample can include more than one inventory.
I found a straight stretch with room for a full inventory of fires. The peak is now **3,038 XP/min**. I’m testing bank reloads with yews first, then repeating the best setup with magic logs.
The banked-yew test is progressing: one full inventory is stored and the second is nearly ready. This will measure whether the faster fires and reloads can beat the magic-log peak.

The yew test confirmed fast burning, but stalls near the end of each row erased the gain. I’m shortening each burn run and reloading sooner. That should preserve the fast section when I use magic logs.
Firemaking has reached **99**. I’m still training for the rate score: the first magic inventory is nearly full, and the remaining time is going into banked supplies and burst tests.
Woodcutting is now **99** too. I’m preparing a shorter opening burst of magic logs followed by a bank reload, so the next sample can include fast fires from two inventories.

Two full inventories of magic logs are banked, and the shorter opening inventory is nearly ready. This is the main final test: align the first fire to a sample boundary, then reload and continue through the next windows.

The final magic test raised the peak to **3,797 XP/min**. Reusing the same row too soon ran into fires from the previous inventory. I’m checking the remaining logs for one last burst before the timer ends.

Completed 30 minutes.

- **Peak score: 3,797 real-game XP/min**
- Best window: **28:30–28:45**, gaining 189,875 raw XP
- **Firemaking: 99**
- Best approach: magic logs with faster click timing and bank reloads

Tested normal, oak, maple, yew, and magic logs.
I’ll start training immediately, establish a Ranged XP baseline, then test ways to improve the peak rate over the 30 minutes.
The shortbow is earning Ranged XP on Rapid. I’m testing cows next and checking ammunition use; a reliable arrow supply is the first constraint.

I’ve replenished arrows by selling unused starter gear. I’m setting up automatic target switching and arrow recovery, then I’ll compare sustained combat with the Ranging Guild once level 40 is reachable.
Ranged is up to level 27, and the peak has risen from 16 to 44 normalized XP/min. Buildings caused delays around Varrock, so I’ve moved to the open cow field to reduce time between attacks.
The open field worked: Ranged reached level 41 and the peak is now 120 normalized XP/min. I’m earning a small entry-fee bankroll to test the Ranging Guild’s target practice.
I have 462 coins for the guild test, with Ranged at level 46. Arrow recovery kept the initial supply useful through the cow session; I’m now heading to the guild to measure its XP per shot.
The guild is reached. I’m working through its entrance and competition controls; the earlier cow session remains the best measured method so far.

The competition accepted the entry fee and supplied arrows. Its targets sit behind a barrier, so I’m switching to the direct “Fire-at” interaction instead of the helper that tries to walk beside them.
Target practice is working now: the first shot gave 625 raw Ranged XP. I’ve found the required firing position and am testing how quickly successive shots can be completed.

The first full guild round gave 2,750 raw XP—too low to beat the cow peak at this level. I’ve upgraded to a willow shortbow and am gathering enough coins and food for repeated tests without frequent supply stops.
I’m preparing a faster, repeatable guild loop while the bot gathers entry fees. The key test is removing unnecessary pauses between shots and rounds, then checking the fixed 15-second samples.
The bankroll is ready: just over 7,000 coins. I’m returning to the guild for repeated rounds with the upgraded bow and a loop that waits for shot results instead of using a fixed half-second delay.

The improved guild setup is now ahead: 210 normalized XP/min, with Ranged at level 55. Two rounds earned 17,000 raw XP in about 13 seconds. I’ve started a longer run to capture full sampling windows and raise the level further.
Ranged is now level 70, and the peak has reached 335 normalized XP/min. The guild loop is stable. Next I’m testing whether a shorter shot cadence can improve on its roughly seven-second rounds.

The faster cadence cut rounds from about seven seconds to 4.6–5.2 seconds while still completing all ten shots. Ranged is level 78. I’m converting the accumulated tickets into supplies for the final stretch.

Ticket rewards converted into 4,315 coins, enough for another 21 rounds. I also added a coif, leather chaps, and vambraces, and am testing faster entry dialogs plus a firing position closer to the judge.
The peak is now 443 normalized XP/min, and Ranged has reached level 82. The final loop is running continuously; it will recycle ticket rewards if needed and stop at the 30-minute mark.
With 45 seconds left, Ranged is level 84 and the best window remains 443 normalized XP/min. I’m keeping the faster guild method running through the remaining samples.

Completed the 30-minute session.

- **Peak: 443 normalized Ranged XP/min**
- Best window: **22,125 raw XP in 15 seconds**
- Ranged: **1 → 86**
- Best method: Ranging Guild target practice with a willow shortbow and faster shot/dialog handling.

Training has stopped.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get Fishing XP flowing, then test faster approaches against the peak-rate sampler.
The starter net is available. The local fishing notes place the level-1 spots at Draynor; I’m correcting the route there before testing catch and drop timing.
Fishing XP is now coming in at Draynor. Level-up dialogs interrupt catches, so I’m automating their dismissal and inventory clearing, then comparing steady fishing with repeated clicks.
Repeated clicks improved the peak to **130 real-game XP/min**, and Fishing has passed level 20. I’m getting a fly rod and feathers to test trout and salmon, which award more XP per catch.

Fly fishing is much faster: 20 trout/salmon catches gave **30,000 raw XP in about 14 seconds**. I’m stocking enough feathers for sustained tests and keeping a harpoon and lobster pot for a comparison afterward.
The measured peak is **420 XP/min**. I’m testing click intervals over full sampling windows; faster clicking may help, but it can also interrupt the normal catch cycle.
